recommendations.title: Spurious Copper Residue
probable_causes: Contaminated etching solution containing suspended copper particulate.
Solder splatter during wave soldering or hot air leveling (HASL).
inspection_steps: Inspect board surface under 30x darkfield illumination for stray copper flecks.
Determine if particle is encapsulated under solder mask or exposed on top.
repair_actions: Exposed copper flake: remove gently with fine precision tweezers or micro-vacuum.
Embedded particle: route out non-conductive area and re-seal with UV resin.
verification_steps: Visual verification under UV illumination to ensure zero foreign material residues.
safety_notes: UV INSPECTION: Darkfield UV can cause skin erythema with prolonged exposure — use timed exposure cycle.
CHEMICAL: If post-etch rinse is incomplete, residual ammonium persulfate or FeCl3 is corrosive; wear nitrile gloves.
HASL: Hot-air-leveled pads exceed 250°C shortly after processing; allow thermal equilibration before handling.

recommendations.title: Pin-Hole / Via Void
probable_causes: Air entrapment or outgassing during PTH (Plated Through Hole) copper plating.
Moisture absorption in FR4 core before thermal lamination.
Insufficient drill speed or dull drill bit causing rough hole wall topography.
inspection_steps: Perform X-ray micro-computed tomography or cross-sectional metallurgical mount.
Measure pinhole depth relative to pad surface.
repair_actions: Fill surface pinhole with electronic-grade conductive silver epoxy or reflow solder.
Smooth flush with pad surface using thermal flat blade.
verification_steps: Measure contact resistance across via barrel under 1 Amp load test.
safety_notes: CURRENT LOAD: 1-Amp verification testing can cause localized thermal runaway if shorted; use current-limited supply.
EPOXY: Silver epoxy is conductive until fully cured; avoid smearing onto adjacent dielectric spacing.
X-RAY / CT: Micro-CT is ionizing radiation — only trained personnel should operate industrial X-ray sources.
DRILL: Dull drill bits generate FR4 dust (fiberglass irritant); use local dust extraction and respirator mask.

recommendations.title: Mousebite / Trace Edge Erosion
probable_causes: Uneven chemical etching or particulate contamination in acid bath.
Defective photoresist film adhesion along high-density signal tracks.
Air bubbles trapped beneath dry film photoresist during lamination.
inspection_steps: Measure minimum remaining conductor width with calibrated optical graticule.
Check if trace width reduction exceeds 20% of nominal design rule.
repair_actions: If remaining trace width > 80% nominal: clean and apply conformal overcoat to prevent oxidation.
If remaining trace width < 80%: reinforce by soldering tinned copper ribbon jumper per IPC-7721.
verification_steps: Ensure dielectric clearance to adjacent ground plane conforms to IPC-2221 spacing rules.
safety_notes: ACID/CHEMICAL: If reprocessing an etched board, neutralize any residual acid with DI water before handling.
ESD PRECAUTION: Apply conformal coating only on a grounded static-dissipative mat.
OPTICAL: Calibrated optical graticule is fragile — do not touch objective lens with bare fingers.

recommendations.title: Copper Spur / Protrusion
probable_causes: Incomplete chemical etching leaving residual copper spur.
inspection_steps: Measure clearance distance from spur tip to adjacent conductor.
Verify whether minimum electrical clearance has been violated.
repair_actions: Use stereoscopic surgical micro-scalpel to excise unwanted copper protrusion.
Clean debris with vacuum wand and apply insulating lacquer.
verification_steps: High-pot / dielectric withstand voltage test if spur occurs in high-voltage section.
safety_notes: HIGH-VOLTAGE HIPOT: Always discharge DUT after high-pot test; lethal residual voltage can persist.
SHARP TOOL: Surgical micro-scalpel is extremely sharp; use safety sheath when not in use.
DEBRIS: Use closed-tip micro-vacuum for copper shavings; airborne conductive debris can short adjacent boards.

recommendations.title: Trace Disconnection / Open Circuit
probable_causes: Etching over-exposure during inner/outer layer PCB chemical fabrication.
Mechanical scratching or abrasion during manual handling / depaneling.
Thermal expansion fatigue or copper trace fracture under thermal cycling.
Insufficient solder volume on surface mount land (dry joint).
inspection_steps: Conduct micro-continuity probe test along the signal net.
Inspect trace under magnification for hairline cracks or copper delamination.
Check via barrel integrity for barrel crack or knee separation.
repair_actions: Carefully scrape solder mask 2mm on either side of the open break using micro-chisel.
Tin exposed copper trace using fine chisel soldering tip.
Solder 30 AWG insulated polyurethane enameled copper jumper wire across the fracture.
Encapsulate repair site with UV-curable solder mask resin and cure under 365nm UV lamp for 60 seconds.
verification_steps: Verify 0.0 Ω net continuity using digital multimeter.
Perform IPC-7721 tape adhesion test on cured conformal resin.
recommendations.ipc_standard: IPC-7711/7721 Procedure 4.2.1 (Conductor Repair Using Wire Jumper)
safety_notes: ESD PRECAUTION: Use ESD wrist strap and dissipative workbench during trace repair handling.
UV RADIATION: 365nm UV lamps can damage unprotected eyes/skin; wear UV-blocking goggles and gloves during resin cure.
MECHANICAL: Micro-chisel slips can cause lacerations — use tweezers to secure the board and cut AWAY from fingers.
RESPIRATORY: Avoid inhaling rosin-core solder fumes; use local fume extraction.
